element or principle named as subject
compound denoting the pair that moves in the sky

items.question: Which elemental conjunctions render the two sky-moving principles steady?
premises: The preceding verses describe conditions producing swift or mobile states.
This verse states that what is joined with wind is steady.
This verse states that the void together with fire constitutes the two sky-movers in a steady condition.
items.inference: Steadiness of the two sky-moving principles arises from conjunction with wind and from the void accompanied by fire, in contrast to the previously stated mobile conditions.
uncertainties: The exact referents of nabhaścarau in this ritual-physiological context are not fully specified within the verse.
The syntactic relation between śūnyaṃ sāgni and nabhaścarau admits more than one construal.
items.plain_english: But when joined with wind, it is steady; and the void, together with fire, forms the two sky-movers in a steady state.
